top.title: Trent McDuffie proved worth in win over Packers
top.description: The defense led the Los Angeles Rams to a victory over the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night. Chris Shula’s unit forced three takeaways and allowed just 13 points to an opposing offense that can put up points in a hurry. One of the stronger individual performers? Trent McDuffie, one of LA’s prized offseason acquisitions. SumerSports charted 26 passing plays where McDuffie was matched up directly with a Packers receiver. You can’t realistically expect nor ask for better results. 11 plays vs Matthew Golden: 2 targets, 0 catches allowed 6 plays vs Christian Watson: 0 targets, 0 catches allowed 4 plays vs Tucker Kraft: 1 target, 0 catches allowed 3 plays vs Savion Williams: 1 target, 0 catches allowed 2 plays vs Bo Melton: 1 target, 1 catch for 12 yards While the Rams overall had trouble slowing down Watson, who accumulated four first-half receptions for 65 yards and a score before missing the second half due to injury, McDuffie was one of the defenders able to slow down his momentum. Kraft is one of the NFL’s top tight ends and the Rams held him to just three catches for 24 yards. Nate Landman punched out a fumble shortly after one of those receptions for a key defensive takeaway. All-in-all, Jordan Love finished with just 17 completions on 29 passes (59%) for 198 yards, one touchdown, two interceptions, and a passer rating of 62.1. This was an impressive outing for the Los Angeles defense. They limited Love and company even without the team’s other high-profile offseason addition at cornerback, Jaylen Watson. Emmanuel Forbes and Josh Wallace were also stingy in coverage, and that is a positive sign for the remainder of the season. Watson will not return in 2026. Even more positive is the fact the Packers had very little production on the ground. Savion Williams was the most efficient with two carries for 18 yards. Kaleb Johnson was held to 13 yards on eight carries (1.6 average). Byron Young and Myles Garrett each made notable tackles for loss that put Green Bay behind the chains. The Rams have now won five-straight games. Their previous four wins were against weaker competition. The defense is demonstrating they can get the job done even when facing superior quarterback talents and overall stronger opponents. Whether that is true for the offense remains to be seen. What is obvious is that the Rams are a defensive-led team in their current state. On Wednesday, Trent McDuffie proved his worth to a defense that is performing at a high level.

top.title: How Arsenal can expose Man City’s clear weakness to tighten grip on title
top.description: For Manchester City , life after three Champions League-winning midfielders began in earnest against Arsenal in August. They were a goal down after 23 seconds. It was an inauspicious start for Enzo Maresca and Elliot Anderson alike. A reunion with Arsenal on Sunday could be deemed a meeting of managerial midfielders, in Maresca and Mikel Arteta . Each learned from Pep Guardiola , who won the European Cup as a Barcelona player and manager and then in charge of City. But it is also a first Premier League clash since Bernardo Silva and Rodri joined their mentor in decamping from the Etihad Stadium in the summer. Arsenal may not have been sorry to see any go; if Guardiola’s resignation could facilitate an era of dominance from Arteta, and if it may have already begun with last season’s Premier League title, a further factor could be the departures of the City captain and Spain’s World Cup-winning skipper. If City have been confronted with the question of how to replace the irreplaceable, there are different answers. One is simply that it is impossible: they are irreplaceable. Another is: expensively. City committed £326m to three midfield recruits, in Anderson, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Enzo Fernandez . A third is: incoherently, at least so far. Perhaps it is unfair to expect newcomers, both in the dugout and the centre of the pitch, to bring the same cohesion and chemistry as predecessors who became the faces of longevity and continuity, but thus far they have not. A further subplot, arguably, is that Arsenal boast men who represented an alternative line of succession at City: not merely Arteta, Guardiola’s first assistant in Manchester, but Bruno Guimaraes , who was of interest at the Etihad in 2024, but when City chose not to activate his release clause, and Declan Rice , the target who preferred to join Arsenal in 2023. Arguably the England vice-captain was the best central midfielder in the Premier League even with Rodri and Silva; without them, and despite Pascal Gross’ extraordinary start to the season, he definitely is. Arsenal's Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes provide a key advantage over Man City in Bernardo Silva and Rodri's absence (Reuters) But if Arsenal won the war last season, City prevailed in the battles, based around the formidable double act of Silva and Rodri. They faced the Gunners three times; but for Gabriel Martinelli’s injury-time equaliser at the Emirates Stadium, they would have won all three. top.title: Adeyemi, Gavi react after Sabah 1-4 Barcelona: ‘We want to win every match’
top.description: Adeyemi, Gavi react after Sabah 1-4 Barcelona: ‘We want to win every match’ Karim Adeyemi continued his impressive UEFA Champions League form as Barcelona defeated Sabah 4-1 in Baku, while Gavi used the opportunity to underline his importance to Hansi Flick’s squad despite limited playing time this season. Adeyemi replaced the absent Lamine Yamal and delivered another influential performance, scoring after a superb assist from Alejandro Balde. The German forward has now scored in three of Barcelona’s five Champions League matches, strengthening his case as an important attacking option during the club’s demanding schedule. Adeyemi makes the most of Lamine Yamal’s absence Adeyemi’s goal was a positive contribution after Flick trusted him to cover for Yamal, and after the match, the forward said he was pleased to help Barcelona secure the three points. “The goal means a lot to me; I’m pleased for the team that I was able to help secure the win, and we can be happy with the three points,” he began. The German also recognised the challenge of playing away from home and praised Anthony Gordon, who scored twice against Sabah. “It’s always difficult to play away from home; they did a great job and were very motivated. Gordon? He had a very good game; I’m happy for the team and for him, and I hope he keeps scoring more goals.” Karim Adeyemi scored from Alejandro Balde’s assist. (Picture credit: X/@FCBarcelona) Adeyemi then insisted Barcelona have enough quality to cope without their teenage star. “He’s an important player and we have the quality to replace him. At Barça, there must always be replacements, regardless of the position. “We mustn’t rely on anyone or be afraid of anyone. We’re here to win and we want to win every match.” Gavi insists he remains important despite reduced minutes Gavi made his third start of the season against Sabah and played 86 minutes, offering Flick another opportunity to assess the midfielder’s readiness for a greater role. The Spain international acknowledged his importance within the squad while recognising that every player must understand their responsibilities. “Every player is important and everyone needs to be clear about their role. I consider myself important even though I’m not getting as many minutes at the moment, and I must always contribute to the team,” Gavi emphasised. top.title: Scott Gardner proud of the performance despite Fleetwood defeat
top.description: Scott Gardner proud of the performance despite Fleetwood defeat Leeds United Under-21s saw their Jersey Mike's Trophy campaign end in the group stages, after a defeat away at Fleetwood Town on Wednesday evening. The Sky Bet League Two side secured the three points they needed to progress into the knock-out stages, in a game that was all to play for. Scott Gardner's young side had put themselves in with a chance of qualification, but needed a result on the night at the Highbury Stadium, which ultimately they did not get. Speaking after the game, Gardner reflected on a spirited performance from his team. He said: "I thought we were very good and I thought we deserved something from the game. “We looked much more like ourselves tonight compared to the Oldham game and we had enough moments to win it. “But, you know, those moments are key, so if you don't take your chances, senior players find a way. They got two goals in the last 10 minutes, it's a shame for the players, but there’s loads we can take from it. “We knew that there was a respect from them [Fleetwood] and obviously a desire to go through. But our players showed they're more than capable across the board, and hopefully people can see that and the effort they put in. “I'm really proud of this group and how they work every day and wanted to get through, but we have to go again. I am disappointed for them they haven't got the reward of going through, but, you know, credit for how they performed.”

top.title: Knee surgery rules Sinner out of Australian Open
top.description: Jannik Sinner is a five-time Grand Slam champion [Getty Images] Jannik Sinner has been ruled out of the Australian Open in January following an operation on his knee. The 25-year-old Italian, who won the 2024 and 2025 titles at Melbourne Park, has not played competitively since winning Wimbledon on 12 July. In a social media post on Tuesday, world number two Sinner said he had undergone surgery to "improve the condition of my iliotibial band" - a thick band of tissue that runs along the outside of the knee. "We've been in regular touch with Jannik's team and they've confirmed he won't be joining us for the AO [Australian Open] in January following his recent surgery," said Tennis Australia chief executive Andrew Abdo. "Jannik loves competing here in Melbourne and is looking forward to returning for AO 2028. We wish him all the very best with his recovery and look forward to seeing him back on court soon." The 2027 Australian Open main draw starts on 17 January. Sinner's challenge at the 2026 tournament was ended by a five-set semi-final defeat by Novak Djokovic. Sinner was the dominant player for the first half of the season, winning 44 and losing just three of his singles matches. He won five Masters 1000 titles in a row between March and May, becoming the youngest man to complete the 'career Golden Masters', and reclaimed the world's top ranking from Alcaraz along the way. However, he suffered a shock second-round exit at the French Open, with Zverev ultimately stepping up to win his first Grand Slam title. Sinner bounced back on the grass courts, demolishing Novak Djokovic in the semi-finals before coming back from a set down against Zverev in the Wimbledon showpiece. He ended his season in early October, meaning he was unable to defend the points he claimed with title triumphs in China, Vienna, Paris and the ATP Finals at the end of 2025. Zverev went on to win the US Open and secure the year-end number one ranking. top.title: Lions’ late owner Martha Firestone Ford will be on Matthew Stafford’s mind as he watches ex-team play on Thanksgiving
top.description: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford talks with former Detroit Lions owner Martha Firestone Ford. For years, Thanksgiving in the Stafford household meant watching Dad play quarterback for the Detroit Lions. Even after Matthew Stafford joined the Rams, his wife and daughters still had to share him with football. At some point every Turkey Day, he was due at practice. That was Thanksgiving for Stafford. He was either playing in a game or preparing for one. Matthew Stafford throws a pass during the Rams’ 26-13 win over the Packers on Nov. 25, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, Calif. Getty Images This year, the Rams got their work done Wednesday night against the Packers in the NFL’s inaugural Thanksgiving Eve game. For the first time in as long as he can remember, Stafford gets the whole day with his family. And when the Lions come on, his wife and daughters can slide over and make room for Dad on the couch. “I’ll be tuning in just like everybody else,” Stafford said. Except there’s someone he’ll be thinking about when his old team takes the field. Martha Firestone Ford, the Lions’ owner and chair emeritus, died this week . And for all the pleasure Stafford takes in the prospect of a Thanksgiving at home, he said he’ll be “a little heavy-hearted” watching the Lions play. He was a kid from Texas by way of the University of Georgia when the Lions made him the first pick in the 2009 NFL draft. Ford had been part of the organization since 1963, when she and her husband, William Clay Ford, purchased the team. By the time Stafford came along, she had spent nearly half a century welcoming people to Detroit. Detroit owner Martha Firestone Ford, who died this week, plays with Sawyer Stafford, held by her mother Kelly Stafford, before a home game against the Falcons. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect He remembers how warmly she welcomed him and his family. “She’s a special lady to me, to my family, and to that organization to the city of Detroit,” Stafford said. He spent his first 12 NFL seasons there. Along the way, he got to see another side of the woman who had made him feel at home. When her husband died in 2014, Ford took over the Lions herself. The relationship Stafford built with Ford has made her passing all the more painful. Even as he prepared to play the Packers, his heart was with his second family in Detroit. “I’ve reached out to them a little bit,” Stafford said. “Just an unbelievable lady, a great leader, and she’ll be missed.” Even after the trade to Los Angeles, Thursdays in November generally meant practice for the next opponent. It took the NFL putting the Rams and Packers in its inaugural Thanksgiving Eve game Wednesday to give Stafford the first full Thanksgiving off he can remember in years. top.title: Spurs Fall To Trail Blazers In NBA Cup Despite Wemby’s Monster Game: 4 Things We Learned
top.description: Mandatory Credit: Jaime Valdez-Imagn Images Victor Wembanyama did everything he could to carry the San Antonio Spurs to an NBA Cup victory, but it wasn’t enough to overcome the Portland Trail Blazers . Despite a monster 44-point, 16-rebound performance from their superstar, the Spurs fell 116-111 in a game decided by Portland’s efficiency on both ends. Wembanyama was spectacular, shooting 17-30 from the field and adding two blocks while playing 35 minutes. Devin Vassell added 18 points, and Stephon Castle finished with 20 points and nine assists. But San Antonio struggled to find consistency from beyond the arc, connecting on just 10-36 three-point attempts. Just an ugly shooting night. Portland had their own stars show up. Deni Avdija erupted for 33 points, 12 rebounds, and seven assists, while Damian Lillard added 29 points and seven assists. The Trail Blazers also received 16 points from Sidy Cissoko and 11 from Jrue Holiday off the bench. Here are four things we learned from San Antonio’s disappointing NBA Cup loss. 1. Victor Wembanyama Is Nearly Impossible To Stop Wembanyama had an extraordinary performance, and the numbers barely do justice to how much San Antonio relied on him. The Spurs superstar finished with 44 points and 16 rebounds on 17-30 shooting. He also knocked down three three-pointers, converted seven free throws, and recorded two blocks. Portland had no reliable answer for him individually. Wembanyama found easy ways to score and looked like the best player in the world tonight. He also finished with a +2 rating despite San Antonio losing by five points. That is particularly telling when considering how much the Spurs struggled to generate offense outside their primary contributors. The frustrating part for San Antonio is that a 44-point, 16-rebound performance from Wembanyama should normally put a team in an excellent position to win. Instead, the Spurs wasted one of his best performances by failing to provide enough shooting around him. 2. Deni Avdija And Damian Lillard Were A Dynamic Offensive Duo Portland’s victory was built around two outstanding performances from Avdija and Lillard. Avdija was arguably the most complete player on the floor outside Wembanyama, finishing with 33 points, 12 rebounds, and seven assists. He shot 11-21 from the field and 5-8 from three-point range, giving the Spurs problems from virtually every area of the court. Lillard provided another major scoring threat, recording 29 points and seven assists. Although he shot just 7-20 overall, he made five three-pointers and converted all 10 of his free-throw attempts. Together, they combined for 62 points and 14 assists. That production gave Portland enough offensive firepower to withstand Wembanyama’s monster night. Ever since Nathan MacKinnon was injured , which came moments after Cale Makar ‘s injury, the Avs have seemingly tightened up their game. Maybe they were overly reliant on their superstars and needed to get a little uncomfortable. Or maybe it’s what Jared Bednar talked about weeks ago, that veteran teams sometimes need a little time to get going. Either way, something is working. The Avalanche got Makar back against the Montreal Canadiens on Wednesday and went on to complete a 6-0 rout of one of the best teams in the Eastern Conference. Makar wasn’t the biggest difference-maker in this one. It wasn’t even Mackenzie Blackwood , who helped the Avs record their third consecutive shutout win on home ice by making 27 saves. It was Devon Toews . The Avalanche’s veteran defenseman has been magnificent this season and continued that trend against the Canadiens. Toews scored two of Colorado’s six goals. He also played 22:59, including 4:50 on the power play. One of his goals came on the man advantage where he’s currently quarterbacking the top unit. top.title: Maxx Crosby sends clear message on Deshaun Watson ahead of Browns showdown
top.description: Credit: Mitchell Leff/Jared C. Tilton via Getty Images Maxx Crosby has made his feelings clear on Deshaun Watson ahead of the Las Vegas Raiders’ clash with the Cleveland Browns, describing the quarterback as a major threat. The Raiders are preparing for their first primetime appearance of the season, with their defence facing the challenge of containing Watson and his ability to make plays both through the air and on the ground. Watson impressed in his previous outing against the Houston Texans, completing 25 of 40 passes for 312 yards while adding 49 rushing yards and a touchdown on eight carries. Maxx Crosby explains why Deshaun Watson poses a major threat Crosby knows the Raiders will need to be at their best to limit the Browns quarterback, who has shown he can create problems even when a play breaks down. Speaking to reporters , the Las Vegas defensive star praised Watson’s physical attributes and ability to lead Cleveland’s offence. “[Watson is] a dual-threat guy,” Crosby said. “He’s had a lot of success in this league. He’s got a really strong arm, tough, mobile, and can make a lot of off-schedule plays. He can obviously process as well. “He’s a really good quarterback [and] is leading those guys, and I’ve got a lot of respect for his game. We know it’s another challenge. He’s a really good guy, and for us, we’ve got to be at our best to slow him down and mess up his day.” Crosby also admitted the Raiders are excited about playing under the primetime spotlight, although he knows the pressure is on his team to deliver. “We’re fired up,” he added. “It’s awesome. You want to play on the biggest stages against the best team.” The defensive end described the situation as “do or die” for Las Vegas, with the team desperate to secure a significant win before its bye week. Meanwhile, former Browns player Hanford Dixon believes Cleveland should win the matchup but admitted he has concerns about Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza. Dixon suggested the rookie has started to look more comfortable in the pocket and is beginning to understand the demands of the position. That gives Cleveland another challenge to consider, even with Crosby making it clear that stopping Watson will be a major priority for the Raiders. Mandatory Credit: Jaime Valdez-Imagn Images The Portland Trail Blazers (12-6) have earned the reputation of a dark horse in the West this season. While this may be true, their 116-111 victory against the San Antonio Spurs in Wednesday night’s NBA Cup matchup should see them rated as a genuine threat in the West. The Trail Blazers looked dominant against the Spurs. Although the game was neck-and-neck for the most part, Portland’s tenacity and unwillingness to give up eventually broke down San Antonio’s defense, as they outscored the Spurs 32-24 in the fourth quarter to secure the win. Portland’s winning effort was led by the pair of Deni Avdija and Damian Lillard , who combined for a whopping 62 points. Aside from them, the late-game contributions of Jrue Holiday and the scoring boost by Scoot Henderson played a vital role in sealing the deal. The Spurs also had some standout performers, with Victor Wembanyama (44 PTS, 16 REB, 2 BLK) and Stephon Castle (20 PTS, 6 REB, 9 AST) outscoring the Blazers’ duo with a combined 64 points. Unfortunately, with solid contributions across the board, Portland would not be denied this win. In light of this, we examine and rate the performance of each Blazers player that participated in the win. Along with his monster 33-point performance to pave the way for Portland, Avdija played some solid defense and placed an incredible amount of pressure on San Antonio’s wings. His efficiency from beyond the arc effectively opened up the game for the Blazers. Given that he also banked in a clutch three-pointer to give Portland a sizable lead, the forward was the driving force behind the team’s success. top.description: Barcelona's Brazilian forward #09 Gabriel Jesus reacts during the UEFA Champions League match between Sabah and Barcelona at the Baku Olympic Stadium in Baku on November 25, 2026. (Photo by Igor IVANKO / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Gabriel Jesus was happy with his goal but not his performance in Barcelona’s 4-1 win over Sabah in the Champions League on Wednesday. The summer signing was in the starting XI for the match as Hansi Flick rotated his side and did get on his scoresheet. Speaking afterwards, Jesus explained why he had found it tough going in Baku against Sabah. “It’s always difficult, the Champions League is. Obviously, everyone can talk about Barça, but if Sabah is in the competition, it’s because they have a good team. We have played some players who haven’t participated as much in recent matches. We have won, I’m happy about the goal but not so much about my performance. Happy, but I hope I can keep helping the team,” he told reporters. “Normally, when players who haven’t been playing as much, it’s hard to find the rhythm, and at the start of the match I think it showed. This is part of the game.” Jesus admitted he’s well aware that he’s a squad player but he’s still hoping for more minutes as the season progresses. “We are here to help Barça become a better team. I understand my situation and try to stay in shape. Training without playing is complicated, but that’s how it is. We try to help, the decision is Flick’s. top.title: Navajo Stirling & Carlos Ulberg Make Decision on Future UFC Fight
top.description: Navajo Stirling Carlos Ulberg UFC Getty UFC light heavyweight teammates Navajo Stirling and Carlos Ulberg have made a decision about a future fight against each other. Ulberg is the current UFC light heavyweight champion, while Stirling is one of the top contenders in the weight class following his KO win over Jiri Prochazka at UFC Qatar — the same man whom Ulberg beat to collect the title back in April at UFC 327. These two men should fight for the belt next. But with both fighters training at City Kickboxing in Auckland, New Zealand, it makes things a bit more difficult. Now, we know what their decision is. Navajo Stirling Won’t Fight Carlos Ulberg According to CKB head coach Eugene Bareman , the team has decided that Stirling will not fight Ulberg, even if the belt is on the line. “Boys from the same gym don’t fight. We’ve had this agreement from the very beginning of the gym. Some things are bigger than fighting. Friendship and the bond you’ve built with someone are bigger than fighting,” Bareman said. 🚨🏆Eugene Bareman confirms Carlos Ulberg and Navajo Stirling will NOT fight each other for the title: “Boys from the same gym don't fight. We've had this agreement from the very beginning of the gym. Some things are bigger than fighting. Friendship and the bond you've built… pic.twitter.com/Hrzfbr8lwi — Home of Fight (@Home_of_Fight) November 26, 2026 Team Holding Navajo Stirling Back Based on this decision, it seems like Stirling is being held back from doing what he set out to do when he first became an MMA fighter, which is to win the UFC title. There is no doubt that this is a difficult situation for the team and for both fighters involved, because MMA is partly a team sport. But it’s also an individual sport, and the team choosing for these two not to fight each other is holding Stirling back from testing himself against the champ. For Ulberg, this is an easier decision, because as the champion he has other contenders whom he can fight, such as Magomed Ankalaev. But for Stirling, the decision not to fight his teammate is one that could change the trajectory of his entire career. It will be interesting to hear what UFC president Dana White has to say about this, because he’s always said in the past that MMA fighters need to look out for themselves, and in this case, it looks like the team is putting Ulberg first. How Rodman performed in the season that unfolded afterwards only served to justify the deal. From rising temperatures to Democratic control of the US Congress to another total solar eclipse, here are five events to look out for in the coming year. El Nino in a hotter world With an El Nino cycle among the strongest ever observed, 2027 could break new global temperature records. El Nino is a naturally occurring weather phenomenon that emerges from the Pacific approximately every two to seven years. It shifts global rain patterns and brings higher temperatures to much of the planet, exacerbating rising temperatures caused by climate change. This year’s El Nino has already impacted maize in central America, fishery catches in Peru and sugar and rice production in Southeast Asia. But for harvests in some regions and food price spikes, “the worst is probably yet to come,” according to Kaveh Zahedi, of the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization. After their sweeping November midterm victory, Democrats plan an early push to ease living costs, including restoring Affordable Care Act insurance subsidies, reversing cuts to health care and rolling back Trump’s tariffs. They also want to end the war in Iran, which has driven up fuel prices. Hakeem Jeffries, poised to become the first black House speaker, will oversee a majority able to put Democratic bills to a vote, shape federal spending and use budget negotiations to press for concessions. nigeria.title: Trump, NATO chief urge Russia not to ‘expand’ Ukraine war
nigeria.description: US President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte urged Russia not to “expand the war” in Ukraine, in a joint statement issued Wednesday after meeting in Florida. The “outstanding” and “very impactful” meeting focused on the wars in Ukraine and Iran, said the statement issued by the White House after the closed-door talks at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort. “We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible,” the statement added. The joint appeal by Trump and Rutte comes despite the US leader describing Russian President Vladimir Putin as “my friend” during a meeting in China last week. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has taken issue with Trump’s comments on Putin. “For us, he is a killer,” Zelensky told CNN. Rutte was asked about Trump’s comments in an interview with Fox News’ “Fox & Friends” on Wednesday. “What President Trump is doing, also in the meeting in Shenzhen, is testing Putin,” the NATO secretary general said. “How serious is he? Is he willing to come to the negotiating table? Is he willing to really engage in talks. “So let’s keep the pressure on. I think it is working, and we have to keep that going.” Trump, accused by critics of siding with Moscow over Kyiv, said following his meeting with Putin that the Russian leader wants to see the war end by “diplomatic means.” The Florida meeting comes as European nations have expressed a desire to join preliminary talks that have so far only included Ukraine, the United States and Russia. Rutte said any agreement is going to have to include security guarantees for Ukraine. “When the war ends, either with a peace deal, preferable, or if not possible, a long-term ceasefire, we need to make sure that Ukraine has the security guarantees going forward,” he said. “But the most important thing here,” Rutte added, “is that we have to make sure that Ukraine has what it needs to keep the fight going, being so successful and putting that maximum pressure on the Russians.” Trump and Rutte also discussed increasing defense spending, which the US president has pressed European powers to do, the joint statement said. The Florida talks also came as Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth is expected to announce in coming weeks a review of the US force presence in Europe. In an email dated November 24, 2026, sent by Yasir Shanono Shehu and Aderinola Shonekan, of the CBN, the apex bank said the measures were designed “to address seasonal demand pressures and improve orderly access to US$ cash for end users.” The apex bank stated: “All licensed BDCs (please see attached) may access US$ cash for FX purchased at the NFEM through the Authorised Dealer Banks (ADBs) with which they hold accounts, and the CBN will support ADBs with any cash requirements to meet the demand of their BDC clients.” Under the new arrangement, “the approved licensed BDCs may receive up to 100% of an approved FX purchase in US$ cash from the ADB where they hold their settlement account.” The CBN added that “the weekly purchase cap is temporarily increased from USD 150,000 to a maximum of USD 1 million per BDC.” BDCs are required to submit requests through the BDC FX Purchase Tracker (FXBT), while authorised dealer banks are expected to acknowledge requests same day and confirm or reject them on the portal, stating reasons for any rejection. nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu’s promise to cut transport fares by about 40 per cent is receiving deserved attention, but Nigerians will judge it by its genuine impact on the common people. The target, announced under the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme (NACTP) for 2027–2031, applies only to “participating routes”. Nigerians need a nationwide programme. The package centres on an agreement with Chinese manufacturer Yutong Bus Co. Ltd to supply 300 compressed natural gas buses. The first 100 are expected in Lagos by December 2026; subsequent buses are to be assembled through YP Automobiles at the former Leyland plant in Ibadan. The Presidency says this will support jobs, technical skills and local manufacturing. It also cites 2,000 additional CNG refuelling infrastructure units. The reasoning is simple: cheaper fuel should reduce operators’ costs and, hopefully, fares. But 300 buses cannot transform road transportation in a country of more than 230 million people. Private bus, minibus and taxi owners must not be pushed aside by government-subsidised fleets. Government should offer conversion loans, reliable gas supplies and affordable maintenance. Otherwise, only a few corridors may benefit. Rural transport deserves equal attention. Farmers contend with poor roads, expensive fuel and costly journeys from farms to markets. An urban passenger bus scheme will do little for them. CNG support must reach rural transporters and produce-haulage operators. Feeder roads and market links need investment too. Cheap movement of food is part of alleviating hardship. The timing of this policy is politically awkward. In May 2023, Tinubu announced that the petrol subsidy was gone. The pump price, about N185 a litre, quickly rose above N500; by September 2026, NMDPRA data showed prices around N1,300–N1,450. After three and a half years of hardship, a 40 per cent fare promise ahead of the 2027 elections looks to some like a campaign sweetener. Only sustained implementation can dispel that suspicion. India’s successful PM-eBus Sewa scheme combines private bus operation with public support for depots, charging infrastructure and payment security in its 10,000-bus programme. Brazil’s transport-voucher system requires employers to help meet workers’ commuting costs. Nigeria should explore lessons from these equally heavily populated countries. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). Veteran Nollywood actor Chief Dr Pete Edochie and his wife, Barrister Mrs Josephine Edochie, at a church service. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Chief Dr Pete Edochie is survived by his beloved wife of over five decades, Barrister Mrs Josephine Edochie, their six children—Leo, Adam, Linc, Jean, Yul, and Eva Edochie (with Linc and Yul following closely in his acting footsteps)—as well as his siblings, grandchildren, and extended family. entertainment.description: Williams Alamu marks his B.Sc. First-Class Honours graduation in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. There was a time when Williams Alamu would rather not sit an examination than risk getting a grade he wasn’t happy with. A B or a C in his Cambridge A-levels felt like a possibility he wasn’t ready to entertain, so he didn’t write the exams. A few years later, at 23, he has graduated from the University of Ibadan with a B.Sc. in Statistics, First-Class Honours and a CGPA of 3.65/4.0. Somewhere along the way, he decided that fear was no longer going to make his decisions for him. When Williams got into UI, he had a rather ambitious plan: become the Best Graduating Student in his faculty. Getting there would require more than good intentions. There were 5:30am wake-ups, difficult Statistics courses, friends who became unofficial tutors, a ChatGPT Pro subscription in 300 level, job offers he turned down and one Demography exam that kept him awake for 36 hours. University, as it turns out, came with quite a few plot twists. In this interview with BellaNaija, Williams takes us through the habits, people and decisions that shaped his academic journey. He also tells us whether he got that coveted top spot, what he learnt from the opportunities he put on hold, and what he would tell another student hoping to graduate with First-Class Honours. If that’s a goal you’re working towards, you may want to take notes. Literally or otherwise. Williams Alamu celebrates graduating with First-Class Honours in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. At what point did you realise you were chasing a record-breaking grade? Was it a goal from Day 1, or did it evolve? It was a goal from day one, actually. When I gained admission into the University of Ibadan, I already had my mind set on graduating as the Best Graduating Student in my faculty. I knew becoming the overall Best Graduating Student in the university would require an extraordinary amount of work, but I felt being the best in my faculty was something I wanted to work towards. And, of course, that would also mean graduating as the best student in my department. The motivation behind that goal goes back to shortly after secondary school, when my parents enrolled me in a Cambridge A-level programme. I went into it hoping to achieve three A-stars, but Chemistry was a major struggle. As the examinations approached, I became increasingly worried about my performance. I think I was more afraid of not meeting my own expectations than I was of the examination itself. The thought of getting a B or C frightened me so much that I eventually decided not to sit for the examinations. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? sports.title: Knee surgery rules Sinner out of Australian Open
sports.description: Jannik Sinner is a five-time Grand Slam champion [Getty Images] Jannik Sinner has been ruled out of the Australian Open in January following an operation on his knee. The 25-year-old Italian, who won the 2024 and 2025 titles at Melbourne Park, has not played competitively since winning Wimbledon on 12 July. In a social media post on Tuesday, world number two Sinner said he had undergone surgery to "improve the condition of my iliotibial band" - a thick band of tissue that runs along the outside of the knee. "We've been in regular touch with Jannik's team and they've confirmed he won't be joining us for the AO [Australian Open] in January following his recent surgery," said Tennis Australia chief executive Andrew Abdo. "Jannik loves competing here in Melbourne and is looking forward to returning for AO 2028. We wish him all the very best with his recovery and look forward to seeing him back on court soon." The 2027 Australian Open main draw starts on 17 January. Sinner's challenge at the 2026 tournament was ended by a five-set semi-final defeat by Novak Djokovic. Sinner was the dominant player for the first half of the season, winning 44 and losing just three of his singles matches. He won five Masters 1000 titles in a row between March and May, becoming the youngest man to complete the 'career Golden Masters', and reclaimed the world's top ranking from Alcaraz along the way. However, he suffered a shock second-round exit at the French Open, with Zverev ultimately stepping up to win his first Grand Slam title. Sinner bounced back on the grass courts, demolishing Novak Djokovic in the semi-finals before coming back from a set down against Zverev in the Wimbledon showpiece. He ended his season in early October, meaning he was unable to defend the points he claimed with title triumphs in China, Vienna, Paris and the ATP Finals at the end of 2025. Zverev went on to win the US Open and secure the year-end number one ranking. sports.title: Lions’ late owner Martha Firestone Ford will be on Matthew Stafford’s mind as he watches ex-team play on Thanksgiving

For years, Thanksgiving in the Stafford household meant watching Dad play quarterback for the Detroit Lions. technology.description: Indian politicians have proposed that AI could take a major role in citizens’ lives, partly through pervasive surveillance. Prime Minister Narendra Modi last week spelled out his vision for an AI-based app that would collect data about children as they grow and analyze it to determine their aptitude for different types of study or careers. Modi suggested that parents of three-year-old children should enter data about their offspring’s activities and accomplishments into a government-run system that is also accessible to teachers and even a child’s friends. Those records, the PM suggested, will “help identify children's interests and aptitude from an early age and redirect them in the study of their choice in future.” That’s not an entirely creepy idea, because gaining access to India’s top tertiary institutions requires students to pay a hefty fee to sit for entrance exams. A 178-page tender seeks bidders to build a system that uses the state’s Family ID – a unique identifier for each household – to link data held by multiple agencies so it can be put to work in a dozen AI use cases. Critics have pointed to vague wording in the tender as potentially allowing the UP government to link this system to other agencies – a matter of concern given Indian state and national governments have implemented internet shutdowns to stop protestors from communicating on social media services and messaging apps. An app for teachers will advise them on how to create custom content to meet students’ needs. Healthcare workers would also get an app to help them make recommendations during patient visits. Citizens get natural language interfaces to a system that offers advice on how to identify and access government services and schemes. UP wants to drive these apps with self-hosted open-weight models, and to use only anonymized datasets. technology.description: The United States Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s plan to launch a million datacenter satellites. The regulator on Wednesday published an order [PDF] allowing SpaceX to operate a “Non-geostationary satellite orbit (NGSO) constellation of 1,000,000 satellites deployed into orbital shells each spanning 50 km at altitudes from 500 to 1,002 km and in 30-degree inclinations and sun-synchronous inclinations.” The order requires SpaceX to ensure its satellites’ radios don’t interfere with US government systems which use the 28.6-29.1 GHz band and requires the company to stick to operating within the parameters it files with the International Telecommunications Union. SpaceX asked the FCC to waive its rule requiring the atmospheric disposal of dead satellites orbiting at 2,000 km or less. Elon Musk’s company asked for “flexibility to dispose satellites operating above 600 km altitude into Earth disposal orbits or heliocentric orbits.” The FCC found SpaceX did not provide enough information to let it assess if proposed “alternative disposal methods” are compliant with regulations, so deferred its decision on the waiver request. “SpaceX must file an application for modification of this authorization and provide sufficient justification for any requested waiver(s) of the Commission’s rules,” the order states. The company must also file twice-yearly reports about “conjunction events” – moments when its satellites get dangerously close to each other, or other orbiters. Whether orbiting datacenters are feasible, make sense, or will ever pay for themselves, remain open questions. Analyst firm Gartner has described the idea as “ peak insanity .” Google thinks orbiting datacenters become viable if launch costs fall to $200/kg, which would mean SpaceX needs to launch its massive Starship 1,800 times. SpaceX’s assumptions assume near-daily launches, far better than its current cadence of a launch every three days or so. Fundamental networking research must also come to fruition to handle the amount of traffic large constellations of orbiting datacenters will create. Terrestrial manufacturing capacity will also need to increase to build all those satellites. Elon Musk’s companies and Intel have planned a giant new fab to make that possible, without explaining how the supply chains behind chip manufacturing will scale to make it feasible. That's a notable omission given that semiconductor supply chains are already extremely strained. Approval for SpaceX is therefore nice but in no way a roadmap to a million datacenter satellites. Google, ironically, is a little further along than SpaceX, having launched a test sat in October and last week announcing it has hired Amazon founder Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin to launch a larger satellite carrying the equivalent of a full datacenter rack in early 2029. technology.description: Four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. The first-of-its-kind experiment worked beautifully as the solar-powered space probe slammed into asteroid Dimorphos, permanently altering its trajectory. Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission. The spacecraft released some 10 billion joules of energy as it impacted Dimorphos in September 2022 at more than 13,700 mph (6.14 kilometers per second), shortening the asteroid's 12-hour orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, 25 times the most conservative expectation. technology.title: The security of US water systems is even leakier than we thought
technology.description: American water systems are even less secure than we thought, according to a study of 236 technology vendors that provide gear to US drinking water, wastewater, and industrial water systems. The federal government has issued 4,014 security advisories for industrial control systems and cataloged 1,792 vulnerabilities known to have been exploited in cyberattacks. A new index, called Water Supply Chain Watch and published by exposure management firm Securin, however, found almost twice as many vulnerabilities as public records identified – including 20 exploited flaws that weren't even in the federal government's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The security provider compared data on water-tech vendors with records from the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the FBI, and WaterISAC, drawing on CISA advisory data through November 20 and KEV catalog entries through November 23. It found that federal water advisories hit their highest level this year since 2020. However, the volume of security alerts isn't a reliable predictor of real-world attacks, the researchers noted. Five vendors – Rockwell Automation (58), Advantech (48), Schneider Electric (35), Siemens (26), and ABB (24) – account for 191 of the 376 water-tagged security advisories. The No. 2 firm, Advantech, accounted for the highest number of vulnerabilities rated critical, but none of the CVEs in its advisories appear in CISA's KEV catalog. Unitronics, on the other hand, accounted for only two water-tagged security advisories, but at least 75 of its controllers were compromised between November 2023 and January 2024 by attackers taking advantage of default or missing passwords. The report also highlights another disconnect between water-related CVEs and real-world cyberattacks, which don't always require attackers to exploit software bugs. The July intrusions, which security researchers suspect were the work of Iran-linked attackers , targeted more than 100 water systems , with incidents reported across at least 12 states , and involved poorly secured internet-connected controllers . technology.title: Huawei and crew tout homegrown EDA tools to overcome China’s fab deficit
technology.description: Chinese telecom and IT giant Huawei boasted about its advancements in domestic electronic design automation (EDA) software this week, which it needs to accelerate the adoption of homegrown chip manufacturing. EDA is an umbrella term for software, hardware, and services essential to the planning, design, and production of modern chips. Today, Cadence Design Systems, Synopsys, and Siemens dominate the industry, but US export controls have restricted Huawei and other blacklisted Chinese businesses' access to their tools. The US blacklisted Huawei back in 2019 over concerns the telecommunications equipment giant could be forced to inject backdoors into its gear. Unable to access top EDA tools, Huawei’s chip division, HiSilicon, was forced to develop its own with the help of Phlexing Technology. This week, Phlexing chairman Qing He detailed the company’s efforts to bring new EDA tools to support Huawei’s so-called Tau Scaling Law design philosophy. “Tau EDA is the domestic EDA tool chain for Tau chips. It comes from a long, close partnership with Huawei,” he said. We discussed the tech earlier this year, but in a nutshell, it involves using advanced packaging, specifically 3D hybrid bonding, to achieve higher transistor density for a given area. The TSMC of China, Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC), is still years behind Taiwan, South Korea, and the US on process technology. It currently has the ability to mass-produce chips on the equivalent of a 7 nm process. For comparison, TSMC began producing 5 nm-class products in 2020 and commenced mass production of 2 nm-class chips in late 2025. So, Huawei aims to use 3D packaging to close the gap, but for this to happen, it first needs tools capable of designing such chips, and that’s just what Phlexing claims to have done with its GloryBolt and GloryEX platforms. “Traditional EDA has long handled only single processes. Tau EDA needs to integrate and decompose multiple processes,” He said. “Coupling multi-scale, multi-structure, and multi-physics issues called for new analysis tools.” This, He says, culminated in the co-development of a process design kit (PDK) with Huawei beginning in 2024. These technologies have now gone live. The development comes as Huawei looks to bring larger, more capable processors to market. We previously discussed the company’s latest developments around AI accelerators, near packaged optics, networking, and rack systems. Many of these advancements will depend on multi-die chip packages, enabled by EDA tools, like those built by Phlexing. ®

science.title: The defence tech revolution is changing how we innovate
science.description: Cpl Aaron J Stone/UK Ministry of Defence Only five years ago, defence technology start-ups had little choice but to wait for government funding to build and test their inventions – often in complex, multi-year programmes. No longer, however: Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022 has prompted such a fast, furious response that military innovation timescales have shrunk dramatically. “Ukraine is becoming a real-world lab for military innovation, and it’s innovating at a pace greater than anything that we’ve seen previously,” says Ola Fashade, an air vice-marshal in the Royal Air Force and director of military digitalisation and the rapid AI delivery task force at the UK’s Ministry of Defence (MoD). “Agility and tempo of adaptation is critical. In a contested battlespace, technology that works well on day one, by day eight has become a little muted – and by day twelve it’s probably no longer relevant. And if you don’t adapt over that period, what you have is a very expensive and ineffective bag of steel.” Advertisement That raises the question of how significant this accelerated innovation could become. In September 2026, New Scientist CoLab, sponsored by BAE Systems, brought together leading thinkers and investors from industry, the military and academia to discuss the factors driving this innovation and the lessons that can be transferred to other industries. Staying alive The investment for this step change is coming both from the technology incubators based within military prime contractors – like the Launchpad incubator at BAE Systems – and from a host of venture capital (VC) companies worldwide. “The idea behind Launchpad is to forge an ecosystem that gets technology from defence start-ups into the front line quicker, or into spinouts, before they run out of money and die,” says David Ewing, head of technology commercialisation at BAE Systems. In addition, VC funding is seeing a raft of new multibillion-dollar military tech players, dubbed neoprimes, that complement the work of the primes on bigger-ticket battlespace items. The poster child for the neoprimes, says Samuel Burrell, a partner at the pan-European VC firm Expeditions Fund, is the nascent British air defence start-up Cambridge Aerospace, which reached a valuation of $3.4 billion with little but a convincing tech narrative: “They had no battlefield data, no product – just a compelling team and an idea on paper.” It wasn’t all talk: Cambridge Aerospace has begun delivering its Skyhammer air defence missile for taking out Shahed-type drones and cruise missiles. A solid-rocket-motor-powered ballistic missile interceptor, Starhammer, will ship in 2027. science.title: Seeking Refuge on Resolution Island
science.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Seeking Refuge on Resolution… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search In the late 1800s, wildlife conservationists in New Zealand were recognizing how predators such as stoats , brought to the country to control other nonnative animal populations, were becoming a threat to native birds. Naturalists at the time surmised that some of the nation’s islands could serve as sanctuaries where endemic species could persist, free from the voracious newcomers. Resolution Island, located in the Fiordland region along the rugged southwest edge of New Zealand’s South Island, was one of the first eyed for this purpose. Conservationist Thomas Henry Potts proposed in 1872 that the island could be a place where “wingless species, and birds of feeble powers of flight, might there find a refuge for some of their representatives.” So began an early systematic effort to protect kiwi, kākāpō , and other native birds on Resolution Island, the largest of the approximately 90 islands in Fiordland National Park . This image, acquired with the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 on December 12, 2025, shows the island’s setting amid a landscape of steep-sided valleys carved by glaciers and now inundated by the ocean. The uninhabited island rises from sea level to the summit of Mount Clerke at 1,069 meters (3,507 feet). Its diverse habitats and vegetation communities range from bogs and wetlands near the coast to widespread podocarp forests at middle elevations to tussock grasslands in the subalpine and alpine areas. Offshore, the Taumoana (Five Fingers Peninsula) Marine Reserve protects estuarine and wave-exposed rocky reef habitats at the entrance to Dusky Sound, east of Five Fingers Peninsula. Farther into the sound, Pigeon Island was the onetime home of Richard Henry, who was named caretaker of Resolution Island after it was designated a reserve in 1891. In what some have called a “ landmark effort ,” Henry spent years transporting more than 700 birds, mostly kiwi and kākāpō, by rowboat to Resolution and other would-be island sanctuaries nearby. In 1900, however, people began spotting mustelids on Resolution. It turns out the island is within swimming distance for animals such as stoats. Henry was intent on trapping the interlopers but eventually abandoned the project and moved on to caretaking work on another island. The spirit of his efforts lives on, though. A Department of Conservation program started in 2008 aims to control stoat populations and bolster native species on Resolution. It is often called the "Cold Moon" in reference to the frigid temperatures that prevail in the Northern Hemisphere around the time of its rising, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . December's full moon will also occur close to perigee — the moon's closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit — giving rise to a spectacular supermoon. A supermoon can appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than a full moon at its farthest point from Earth (also known as a micromoon).. According to the late, great astronomer Fred Espenak , the Cold Moon will be just 221,667 miles (356,740 kilometers) from Earth when it turns full, making it the closest supermoon of 2026! When to see the December full moon The full Cold Supermoon will make for a spectacular sight when it rises over the eastern horizon at sunset on Dec. 23, mere hours before reaching maximum illumination. Remember to use Time and Date's moonrise and moonset tracker for timings specific to your location. Earth's satellite may appear larger than normal while close to the horizon. This is partly because it is near perigee, when it appears subtly larger in the night sky, but also because of a phenomenon called the moon illusion, which tricks us into perceiving the moon to be bigger than it actually is while in the presence of foreground objects. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 25, 1970: NASA's 'wingless' M2-F3 'lifting body' aircraft makes its 1st powered flight ahead of supersonic tests
science.description: null On Nov. 25, 1970, an experimental aircraft called the Northrop M2-F3 made its first powered flight. The M2-F3 aircraft was a heavyweight "lifting body" designed to test its ability to produce most of its lift through its fuselage instead of wings. It's commonly referred to as a "wingless" aircraft. After Air Force test pilot Bill Dana took the M2-F3 on three unpowered glide test flights, he did the first powered flight, too. Dana soared to an altitude of 45,000 feet during this flight, which lasted just over 6 minutes. He didn't break the sound barrier this time, but he did on later flights. The M2-F3 flew a total of 27 missions in its three-year flight history. Its top speed was 1.6 times the speed of sound, and its top altitude was 71,500 feet. NASA's M2-F3 lifting body drops from its carrier plane during a test flight in 1970. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered In the late 1960s and early 1970s, NASA was investigating lifting bodies as an approach to both new aircraft and what future spacecraft, and as its number suggests, the M2-F3 was not the first of its kind. In fact, the M2-F3 was a rebuilt version of its predecessor, the M2-F2 lifting body , after that vehicle crashed in a dry lake bed in California's Mojave Desert during an unpowered test flight. That crash (which appears in the opening of the TV show "The Six-Million-Dollar Man") led to upgrades for a better handling lifting body, NASA said. "When the M2-F2 was rebuilt and redesignated the M2-F3, it was modified with an additional third vertical fin – centered between the tip fins – to improve control characteristics," NASA wrote in an overview . Unpowered glide flights for the M2-F3 began in June 1970, but Dana's flight on Nov. 25 of that year was the first time the vehicle fired up its rocket engine to test its controls under powered flight. One vital upgrade on the vehicle was a set of reaction control thrusters to help maintain its orientation. "A reaction jet control system, similar to thrusters used on orbiting spacecraft, was also installed on the M2-F3 to obtain research data about their effectiveness for vehicle control," NASA wrote . "As the M2-F3’s portion of the lifting body program neared an end, it evaluated a rate command augmentation control system and a side-arm control stick similar to side-arm controllers now used on many modern aircraft." If you want, you can see the M2-F3 vehicle today. NASA donated it to the Smithsonian Institution. It is now hanging at the National Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C. Want more space history? The U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) just granted SpaceX approval to deploy one million of its Starmind AI data-center satellites in orbit. "This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America's leadership and growth," FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said today (Nov. 25) in a statement announcing the approval. AI has become central to SpaceX's business plans and identity over the past year or so. For example, the company has said that it's eyeing a "total addressable market" of $28.5 trillion over the long haul — and nearly $23 trillion of that is in "enterprise AI applications." Starmind is key to those lofty ambitions. SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk believes that the future of AI compute is in space, where energy (from the sun ) is unlimited and there are no land-owning neighbors to lodge NIMBY complaints. SpaceX aims to launch the first of its Starmind satellites in the third quarter of 2027. The spacecraft will fly on the company's fully reusable Starship megarocket, which has deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink satellites on its most recent two test flights . Those 52 spacecraft are the vanguard of another enormous constellation: Musk has said that the next-gen Starlink network will eventually consists of about 100,000 satellites . The planned numbers for Starlink and Starmind are truly mind-boggling. To put them into perspective: Since the dawn of the space age in 1957, humanity has launched a total of just 28,000 satellites, give or take a few hundred. And the biggest constellation ever operated to date, the current iteration of Starlink, consists of about 11,000 spacecraft. These coming buildouts will require an enormous number of launches. Starship can carry a maximum of 60 V3 Starlink satellites per launch, for instance, so it will take about 1,700 liftoffs just to assemble that network (and more to maintain it, as the operational life of each satellite is expected to be about five years). Putting so many satellites into orbit also raises the risks of collisions. SpaceX has proven to be extremely proficient in this regard with its current Starlink satellites, which can detect and avoid potential collisions autonomously. But more evasive maneuvers will be required as space gets more and more crowded. SpaceX isn't the only company that aims to operate data centers in space; Cowboy Space , Starcloud, Blue Origin and Google, among other companies, have voiced similar ambitions. science.title: AI’s stunning progress in maths shows how little we understand it
science.description: MARK SYKES/SPL/Alamy There is a story, possibly apocryphal, that when the mathematician G. H. Hardy was about to undertake a dangerous sea voyage, he sent a postcard to a colleague declaring “I have solved the Riemann hypothesis”. Hardy, a staunch atheist, joked that this would prevent his ship from sinking, as God would never let him claim the credit for such a major result without revealing the details of his proof. Hardy would probably be both astonished and aghast that we now have what seems to be a proof of the Riemann hypothesis , a problem that has vexed mathematicians since the 19th century, but that no one yet understands it. The consensus among mathematicians is that the proof, produced with the aid of AI, will hold, but that it will take much more work to make it comprehensible to humans. However you feel about AI, this is a watershed moment, and one that demonstrates just how little we still understand about the capabilities of the technology. As recently as last month, leading mathematician Terence Tao speculated that AI would eventually solve the Riemann hypothesis, but that it may not happen before 2050. Now, some mathematicians are considering whether their hardest and most infamous remaining problems could be settled within months. In a year that has left mathematicians reeling, this may be the knock-out blow. Advertisement This is a watershed moment, and it shows just how little we understand about AI’s abilities For non-mathematicians, the fall of the Riemann hypothesis is harder to interpret. In the past year, AI has seen incredible advances in both maths and coding, but it is perhaps no coincidence that in these arenas, with nothing more than computer code, answers can swiftly be checked and iterated upon, allowing for rapid improvement. When it comes to other human endeavours though, from art to zoology, such verification is far harder, involving either the messy physical world, or unknowable human taste – or both. Whether this verification gap can be closed may become the biggest question of our age. Answers on a postcard, please. What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental? It has been called the hardest problem in mathematics, and now through a combination of human ingenuity and relentlessness, and the computational power of AI, the Riemann hypothesis may have finally been solved

science.description: The New Scientist Book Club read Chris Beckett’s Dark Eden in November Since starting the New Scientist Book Club in May 2023, I have aimed to vary our books as much as possible, moving between science fiction and popular science, older classics and the hottest new titles. Occasionally, though, I’m afraid I let the power go to my head and just choose one of my own personal favourites. That’s what I did in November, with Chris Beckett’s novel Dark Eden , a book I’ve loved ever since it won the Arthur C. Clarke award in 2013. Set on the planet Eden, a sunless world that drifts alone far outside the Milky Way, this follows the descendants of two astronauts who were marooned there over a century earlier. Now numbering 532 people, they tell each other stories of the world their ancestors came from, and struggle to survive on this dark, cold planet as they await the return of “one of those sky-boats with lights on them”. I think it is all wildly imaginative and original and exciting. So it was with some trepidation that I awaited the verdict of my fellow book club members on our Discord channel. I really wanted everyone else to love it, too! Les was similarly gripped. “Started it? I’ve only gone and finished it, haven’t I? science.title: Is The Time Traveler’s Wife the perfect audiobook to experience on shuffle?
science.description: Josie Ford Feedback is our weekly column of bizarre stories, implausible advertising claims, confusing instructions and more Reader Jenny Ozanne writes to tell us of a horrific incident that befell her partner. He had bought Audrey Niffenegger’s novel The Time Traveler’s Wife as a CD audiobook, to listen to on long car journeys. “After a while, he complained that the plot was completely impossible to follow,” writes Jenny. “It was only when I checked his player that I realized he had accidentally set the CD to ‘shuffle’. “ Advertisement Jenny raises two points, which Feedback heartily endorses: “I’m still not sure what’s more impressive: the story’s ability to survive total chronological chaos, or the fact that he listened to three random chapters before suspecting anything was wrong.” Feedback would suggest that The Time Traveler’s Wife might be the ideal novel to experience on shuffle, since the narrative is heavily non-linear. The main character hops uncontrollably back and forth through history. This led us to wonder: would any similarly chrono-displaced stories survive the experience of being played on shuffle, or even be improved by it? We wondered, for instance, about David Mitchell’s Cloud Atlas . This has six stories set in different periods, including a future in which human clones are used as cheap labour, and a more distant future in which everything has gone a bit Mad Max . The stories are linked by characters in later timelines reading about the earlier ones, and by subtle coincidences. What would it be like on shuffle? However, after careful reflection, we realised there is only one correct answer to this, and that is Shane Carruth’s 2004 film Primer , which tells the story of two tech bros who invent a time machine in their garage. At first, they use it to go back in time and make money on the stock exchange, only to become caught up in an escalating web of betrayal and deception as they endlessly rewrite their lives. Primer is so overcomplicated, so mind-wreckingly confusing, that some poor soul once went so far as to draw a diagram trying to convey its timeline. Posted on Reddit by u/Clawz114, the diagram looks like a cross between a metro map and a flowchart of the inner workings of a chemical factory. It is therefore possible that playing the scenes in random order might actually cause the film to make more sense. science.description: null Prime Video’s " Blade Runner 2099 " has arrived with an 8-episode limited series revealing what the "Blade Runner" world looks like 50 years after the events of director Denis Villeneuve’s "Blade Runner 2049." The most obvious change in this depressing dystopia is that replicants are running the LA show after some unmentionable ecological disaster and humans are now the ones relegated to underclass citizens. Starring Michelle Yeoh as a replicant cop named Olwen whose life clock is running out and Hunter Schafer as Cora, a desperate human posing as a replicant blade runner, "Blade Runner 2099" unties these two in a mystery revolving around a rogue blade runner and a deadly secret that might cause their city to implode. science.title: NASA Eyes Crop Candidates for Future Menus
science.description: As NASA prepares for future missions to the Moon and Mars, researchers are studying crops that could provide astronauts with fresh food, nutrition, and variety far from Earth. Such crop variety can help with menus in deep space, something top of mind this week as the nation celebrates Thanksgiving. Strawberries (left) grown in the Space Life Sciences Lab’s controlled environment chamber. Cucumbers (center) and lemon basil (right) grown in a controlled environment chamber at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. NASA Recent testing points to strawberries, cucumbers, and lemon basil as potential options for future explorers. Space crops can absorb carbon dioxide, produce oxygen, and recycle water. These capabilities will become increasingly important as crewed missions extend farther from our home planet. While space crop research advances on Earth, capabilities are also expanding in space. A new investigation from NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division is set to launch to the International Space Station, where the first-of-its-kind prototype growth chamber will provide critical insights for developing crop production systems that could grow crops like these for future Moon Base habitats and Mars missions. Sweet space strawberries Strawberries are among the few sweet fruits under consideration for spaceflight and are nutritious, aromatic, and self-pollinating. Researchers at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida are growing strawberries in flight-like growth chambers to evaluate the potential space crop, and NASA partners at The Australian Research Council Centre for Excellence in Plants for Space also are helping expand knowledge of space strawberries. Researchers at NASA Kennedy, the University of Melbourne, and the University of Western Australia recently tested a wild strawberry against NASA’s leading strawberry candidate, ‘Delizz,’ to see which thrived better under simulated space conditions. Delizz and the wild strawberry produced very different fruits, according to a study published in September in the journal Life Sciences in Space Research. Delizz grew large, red fruit, while the wild strawberry produced small, yellow fruit due to a recessive genetic mutation. But looks are not everything. When grown from a seed, the wild strawberry produced twice as many buds, flowers, and fruit as Delizz. Ultimately, however, NASA’s pick kept its top spot, as the wild strawberry grew too many runners that would take up valuable room aboard a spacecraft. Cucumbers show promise Many crops have been grown in space, but none so far have come from the gourd family. Cucumbers could be the first. Before crops like cucumbers can be grown and eaten in space, they must undergo extensive testing. NASA-funded researchers recently evaluated cucumbers for their growth, yield, and nutrition under spaceflight conditions.
